title: The gérondif and adverbs in -ment
summary: Say how and while with en + -ant (en mangeant, en faisant), and how something is done with adverbs in -ment (lentement, évidemment).
focus: The gérondif and forming and placing adverbs in -ment
content:
## The gérondif: en + -ant

Take the **nous** form of the present, drop **-ons**, add **-ant**, and put **en** in front:

| nous form | gérondif |
|---|---|
| nous mangeons | **en mangeant** |
| nous faisons | **en faisant** |
| nous finissons | **en finissant** |
| nous courons | **en courant** |

Three verbs are irregular: **être → en étant**, **avoir → en ayant**, **savoir → en sachant**.

The gérondif never changes its ending, and it always refers to the **subject** of the main verb: **J'ai vu Paul en sortant** = I saw Paul as *I* was leaving.

## When, how, while: using it

- **Two actions at the same time**: **Il chante en se douchant.** (He sings in the shower.)
- **The means, how**: **Elle a appris le français en regardant des séries.** (She learnt French by watching series.)
- **A condition**: **En partant maintenant, tu arriveras à l'heure.** (If you leave now, you'll be on time.)
- **Tout en** stresses that two things go together, often in contrast: **Tout en étant fatiguée, elle a fini son travail.** (Even though she was tired, she finished her work.)

## Adverbs in -ment

- Feminine adjective + **-ment**: lente → **lentement**, heureuse → **heureusement**, douce → **doucement**.
- Adjective ending in a vowel: masculine + **-ment**: vrai → **vraiment**, poli → **poliment**.
- **-ent → -emment**, **-ant → -amment**, both said *-amment*: évident → **évidemment**, courant → **couramment**.
- Irregular: gentil → **gentiment**, bon → **bien**.

**Placement**: after the conjugated verb (**Il parle lentement**). In the passé composé, short adverbs go between the auxiliary and the participle (**J'ai bien dormi**, **Il a vite compris**); long -ment adverbs usually go after the participle (**Il a répondu poliment**).

vocabulary.example: Je cours tous les matins dans le parc.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I run every morning in the park.

vocabulary.example: J'ai rencontré Lucie en faisant les courses.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I met Lucie while doing the shopping.

vocabulary.example: En étant patient, on obtient beaucoup.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By being patient, you get a lot.

vocabulary.example: Il est parti en sachant qu'il allait pleuvoir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He left knowing it was going to rain.

vocabulary.example: Tout en étant fatiguée, elle a fini son travail.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even though she was tired, she finished her work.

vocabulary.example: Heureusement, le train était à l'heure.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Luckily, the train was on time.

vocabulary.example: Évidemment, il a oublié son parapluie.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Of course, he forgot his umbrella.

vocabulary.example: Il a répondu rapidement à mon message.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Speak softly, the baby is asleep.

quiz.explanation: The means (how I learnt) is a gérondif: en + nous stem + -ant, 'en regardant'.
hints: Start from nous regardons: the stem is regard-.

quiz.explanation: Nous faisons gives the stem fais-, plus -ant: 'en faisant'.

quiz.prompt: Which is the gérondif of avoir?
quiz.explanation: Avoir is one of the three irregulars: en ayant (with être → en étant, savoir → en sachant).
hints: It is irregular, with a y.

quiz.prompt: Le dimanche, nous ___ (courir) lentement au bord du lac.
quiz.explanation: Courir in the present: je cours, tu cours, il court, nous courons, vous courez, ils courent. One r in the present.
hints: Only one r in the present.

quiz.explanation: An adverb is needed to say how she speaks: courant gives couramment (-ant becomes -amment).
Évident ends in -ent, so the adverb is évidemment (-ent becomes -emment).

quiz.prompt: In 'J'ai bien dormi', the adverb bien goes between the auxiliary and the participle.
quiz.explanation: Yes: short adverbs like bien, mal, vite, déjà sit between avoir/être and the participle.
hints: Where is bien in the sentence?

quiz.prompt: Tout ___ fatigué, il a continué à travailler.
quiz.explanation: Tout en + gérondif of être (en étant): even though he was tired.
hints: The gérondif of être is irregular.

quiz.prompt: In 'J'ai vu Paul en sortant', it is Paul who is leaving.
quiz.explanation: The gérondif refers to the subject of the main verb: I saw Paul as I was leaving.
hints: Who is the subject of ai vu?

conversations.title: Running partners
conversations.scenario: Julie and Karim, two colleagues, meet at the coffee machine and talk about running.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Salut Julie ! Tu cours toujours le matin ?
lines.meaning: Hi Julie! Do you still run in the mornings?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui, je cours trois fois par semaine, en écoutant des podcasts.
lines.meaning: Yes, I run three times a week, listening to podcasts.
lines.note: en écoutant: at the same time

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Moi, je cours plutôt le soir, en rentrant du travail.
lines.meaning: I tend to run in the evening, on my way home from work.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pas vraiment. Je cours lentement, mais longtemps.
lines.meaning: Not really. I run slowly, but for a long time.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: C'est en courant régulièrement qu'on progresse.
lines.meaning: It's by running regularly that you improve.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Évidemment ! Et tu prépares le semi-marathon ?
lines.meaning: Of course! And are you training for the half marathon?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui. Heureusement, mon genou va mieux.
lines.meaning: Yes. Luckily, my knee is better.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tu veux courir avec moi dimanche ?
lines.meaning: Do you want to run with me on Sunday?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Avec plaisir ! On pourra discuter tout en courant.
lines.meaning: With pleasure! We'll be able to chat while we run.

listening.text: Heureusement, le bus est arrivé rapidement.
Il a appris l'italien en écoutant la radio.
listening.meaning: He learnt Italian by listening to the radio.

listening.text: Malheureusement, mon frère ne parle pas couramment l'anglais.
listening.meaning: Unfortunately, my brother doesn't speak English fluently.

listening.text: En partant maintenant, vous arriverez à l'heure à la gare.
listening.meaning: If you leave now, you'll get to the station on time.
listening.note: New word: à l'heure = on time.

listening.text: Mon grand-père s'est cassé la jambe en tombant dans l'escalier.
listening.meaning: My grandfather broke his leg falling down the stairs.

listening.text: Tout en étant très occupée, elle répond gentiment à tout le monde.
listening.meaning: Even though she's very busy, she answers everyone kindly.

guide.tip: To build the gérondif, say the nous form out loud and swap -ons for -ant, so nous prenons becomes en prenant.

concept.title: The -ant form without en
concept.markdown: In written French the -ant form also appears without **en**, as the participe présent: **Ayant fini, il est parti.** (Having finished, he left.) **Une femme parlant trois langues.** (A woman speaking three languages.) You will read it more than you say it.

bites.title: en + -ant
bites.rule: Take the nous form, drop -ons, add -ant, put en in front, so nous faisons gives en faisant. Irregular: en étant, en ayant, en sachant.
bites.example: Il travaille en écoutant de la musique.
bites.example_meaning: He works while listening to music.

bites.title: While, by, if
bites.rule: The gérondif says two things happen together, how something is done, or on what condition. Tout en stresses the contrast.
bites.example: C'est en forgeant qu'on devient forgeron.
bites.example_meaning: Practice makes perfect. (Literally: it's by forging that you become a blacksmith.)

bites.title: Adjective plus -ment
bites.rule: Feminine adjective + -ment (lente gives lentement); vowel ending + -ment (vrai gives vraiment); -ent becomes -emment, -ant becomes -amment.

bites.title: Where it goes
bites.rule: After the conjugated verb. In the passé composé, short adverbs go before the participle: j'ai bien dormi, il a vite compris.

sorts.title: -emment or -amment?
sorts.why: Adjectives in -ent give -emment (évidemment), adjectives in -ant give -amment (couramment). Both sound the same.

sorts.title: What does the gérondif express?

items.text: Elle a maigri en faisant du sport.
Il a réussi en travaillant dur.
On s'est rencontrés en attendant le bus.

sorts.why: If the -ant action happens alongside the other, it's simultaneity; if it explains how the result came about, it's the means.

spots.sentence: Il travaille en écoutent de la musique.
spots.why: The gérondif ends in -ant: en écoutant.
Build it on the feminine adjective: lente + -ment.

spots.sentence: Évidament, il a raté le bus.
Nous courrons tous les matins dans le parc.
spots.why: Present tense: nous courons, one r. Courrons with two r's is the futur.

builds.text: Elle chante en faisant la cuisine.
Heureusement, nous sommes arrivés à l'heure.
